correctness.rationale: The original package requires a narrow but genuine scientific correction: its T_n triple count is mislabeled as the number of circuits in the dual matroid. With M represented by [I_n|G_n], minimal supports of C_n^perp are circuits of M, whereas dual-matroid circuits correspond to minimal supports of C_n; the latter code has minimum distance 2·3^(n−1)+1≥7, hence no size-3 circuits. The full corrected RESULT.md replaces this false terminology at the theorem and proof and defines the two matroids explicitly. The surviving final theorem is correct: PG(n−1,3) has L=(3^(n−1)−1)/2 lines through P, each with 3 other points. Every point has two nonzero-vector copies; coordinate axes have a third identity copy. Minimal two-helper recovery iff the target and the two distinct helper projective points lie on a line, producing 12 pairs per line plus four per other axis and one extra for a two-axis line. Axes through a target weight-2 point share one line, yielding the 1_{h=2} correction. Local tripartite helper graphs K_{2,2,2},K_{3,2,2},K_{3,3,2} have matching numbers 3,3,4, and different lines have disjoint helper universes. Parallel target copies add 2 singleton helpers when h=1 and 1 otherwise. Direct independent enumeration of all nonzero vectors, projective lines, generator-column linear dependencies and exact integer counts for every target in n=2,3,4 verified the R2/A2/T formulas and code minima 7,19,55. The arbitrary-n proof is projective combinatorics, not extrapolation from finite checks.
residual_risks: The finite enumeration is not a proof for all dimensions; the all-dimension conclusion uses projective line counts and multipartite graph matching.
The result counts only minimal two-helper recovery sets plus singleton helpers; it does not prove actual storage survival probabilities or improvement to locality one.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality for the *corrected* exact local two-helper and sharp disjoint availability profile, not for the known systematic code, classical projective-line incidences, or general multiset formalism. Mondal–Lee Theorem 3.7 proves the family and codeword weight distribution. Grezet–Hollanti and Silberstein–Zeh discuss deleting simplex columns to obtain locality/availability rather than a fully duplicated nonzero ternary column set with one further copy on each coordinate axis. Jurrius gives simplex primal-subcode support enumerators. A fully read published Resultary theorem treats generalized Hamming support spectra of precisely this same code family, a distinct invariant not determining minimal dual-code local circuits or sharp helper-set packing. General projective incidence and matroid machinery makes the present formulas approachable but none of the inspected primary statements/implications dominates all h-dependent R2/A2 and T formulas. Search noncoverage is not proof of novelty; the inaccessible 2018 high-availability full text and possible unindexed weighted-projective enumeration remain explicit risks.
residual_risks: Highly relevant Silberstein–Zeh DOI:10.1007/s10623-017-0358-0 is subscription-gated; arXiv and lawful OA attempts did not secure the same full paper; authorized Oxford reported vpn_disconnected, and its complete theorem text was not read.
A general weighted-projective-multiset circuit/availability theorem or unindexed thesis could subsume the calculation under another formulation.
Primary article and database searches are bounded and do not prove global priority.

value.rationale: The specific original family is motivated in coding theory and storage repair: it has ordinary locality one because each projective coordinate is repeated, but when a parallel copy is unavailable the number and maximum simultaneous disjoint packing of strictly minimal two-helper alternatives are a separate, natural structural invariant. The exact h=1, h=2 and h≥3 classification identifies a real projective incidence discontinuity from the unique line through two coordinate axes, and the all-n dual-code minimal-triple total T_n gives further relevant combinatorial information. These facts are not the mere known Hamming weight distribution or a small arbitrary instance, nor do they assert unverified reliability improvement. The result can be reused as an exact baseline for availability and erasure-tolerance analysis of replicated projective LCD codes.
residual_risks: Because baseline locality is one, numerical storage advantage depends on an explicit failure model and is not claimed.
No claim is made about locality beyond helper sets of cardinality two or optimized performance of the code family.

limitations: Corrected circuit count refers to generator-column matroid M(G), equivalently support-minimal weight-three dual-code words; it is not a count of circuits of M(G)^*.
Pairwise disjoint optimum concerns sets of at most 2 helper coordinates only, and h refers to projective weight.
Independent tests exhaust n=2,3,4 only; unrestricted proof uses incidence/matching.
